newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Liberia warlord Johnson will not contest elections.
newsitem.headline: Liberia warlord Johnson will not contest elections.

text.p: Liberian faction leader Roosevelt Johnson, the man at the centre of last year's civil war flare-up in the capital Monrovia, says he will not contest promised elections and plans to go into business instead.
Johnson, speaking in Sierra Leone's capital, said that his men were disarming ahead of Friday's deadline under a peace deal brokered by Liberia's West African neighbours.
"I am not going to contest either presidential or parliamentary elections," he told reporters on Sunday.

"I was not a military man. I took up arms only to fight Charles Taylor and the game is over and I am going into private business," he said, repeatedly denouncing Taylor, the man who launched the war in 1989.
Johnson heads the ethnic krahn wing of the ULIMO group, which was set up to block Taylor's bid for power in Liberia.

The peace plan, signed in Nigeria's capital Abuja in August, envisages disarmament and elections, which are scheduled for May. West African leaders have threatened sanctions against any warlord derailing the process.
Taylor and his fellow interim ruling state council vice-chairman Alhaji Kromah, who heads the ethnic mandingo wing of ULIMO, have both announced their intention to stand.
Sometime rivals, they united against Johnson in fighting which held Monrovia hostage and killed hundreds of people in April and May, until West African peacekeepers restored order.
Freed American slaves founded Liberia in 1847. The civil war has killed well over 150,000 people.
